title: UDLF deployment config — Microsoft Sentinel
description: Config for `platform: sentinel`. Sentinel analytics rules (`Microsoft.SecurityInsights/alertRules`, kinds `Scheduled` and `NRT`): schedule, trigger, alert, incident grouping and entity mappings. Written from the ARM API (`2025-09-01`, preview `2025-10-01-preview` for NRT, sub-techniques and `sentinelEntitiesMappings`) rather than the portal. Query lives in `detection_content`.

allOf.$comment: Near-real-time rules are hard-coded to run every minute over the preceding minute and alert on first match, so frequency, lookback and trigger are all meaningless — Sentinel rejects them. The inverse (a scheduled rule requires frequency, lookback and trigger) is left to the deployer, since a partially-authored UDLF config is legitimate and the deployer fills the rest.

schema.description: Sub-schema revision this block was authored against, e.g. `sentinel::0.2.0`.

severity.description: Severity for this deployment. Optional, overrides `detection_context.severity`. Sentinel's own four values: it has no `Critical`, and a UDLF `critical` on the detection renders as `High`.

template.description: Provenance of the Sentinel gallery template this rule came from. Maps to `alertRuleTemplateName` / `templateVersion`; the API returns no version for most rules, so only `uuid` is required.

uuid.description: Template rule UUID, findable in the Sentinel rule repository or analyticsrules.exchange. Maps to `alertRuleTemplateName`.

version.description: Template version in a.b.c form. Maps to `templateVersion`.

scheduling.description: How often the rule runs and how far back it looks. Sentinel allows 5 minutes to 14 days for both, and `lookback` must be at least `frequency`; the deployer enforces the bounds.

nrt.description: Run as a Near Real Time rule: one-minute cadence, alerting on first match. Sentinel cannot convert a rule between NRT and scheduled.

frequency.description: How often the query runs. 5 minutes to 14 days. Maps to `queryFrequency`.

lookback.description: How far back each run searches. 5 minutes to 14 days, and at least `frequency`. Maps to `queryPeriod`.

trigger.description: How many query results are needed to raise an alert. Not valid on NRT rules.

threshold.description: Result count the operator compares against. Maps to `triggerThreshold`.

alert.description: Alert presentation and incident behaviour. Maps to `alertDetailsOverride`, `suppression*`, `incidentConfiguration.createIncident`, `customDetails` and `tactics`. `title` and `description` support `{{columnName}}` substitution.

create_incident.description: Create incidents from alerts this rule raises. Maps to `incidentConfiguration.createIncident`.

suppression.description: How long to wait after firing before the rule may fire again, 5 minutes to 1 day. Boolean `false` disables suppression. Maps to `suppressionEnabled` / `suppressionDuration`.

title.description: Alert display-name format, up to 256 chars with at most 3 `{{columnName}}` placeholders. Overrides the detection title on the alert. Maps to `alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat`.

description.description: Alert description format, up to 5000 chars with at most 3 `{{columnName}}` placeholders. Overrides `detection_context.description` on the alert. Maps to `alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat`.

severity_column.description: Query result column that supplies the alert severity at run time. Maps to `alertDetailsOverride.alertSeverityColumnName`.

tactics_column.description: Query result column that supplies the alert tactics at run time. Maps to `alertDetailsOverride.alertTacticsColumnName`.

tactics.description: Sentinel tactics **in addition to** those the deployer derives from `threat.attack[].tactics`, as Sentinel spells them (`CommandAndControl`). Use it for tactics no technique in `threat` carries, and for the three values with no ATT&CK Enterprise home: `PreAttack`, `ImpairProcessControl`, `InhibitResponseFunction`. Maps to `tactics`.

custom_details.description: Surface query columns as named key/value pairs on the alert. At most 20. Maps to `customDetails`.

key.description: Field name shown on the alert. No whitespace.

column.description: Query result column supplying the value.

dynamic_properties.description: Override built-in alert properties from query columns. Maps to `alertDetailsOverride.alertDynamicProperties`.

property.description: The V3 alert property to override. Severity and tactics are `severity_column` / `tactics_column`, not dynamic properties.

column.description: Query result column supplying the value. Maps to `value`.

grouping.description: How query results become alerts, and how alerts become incidents.

allOf.$comment: Sentinel needs a window and a matching method before it can group alerts into incidents.

event.description: `SingleAlert` groups all query results into one alert; `AlertPerResult` raises one per result.

alert.description: Group alerts from this rule into a single incident. Sentinel caps an incident at 150 alerts.

reopen_closed_incidents.description: Re-open a closed matching incident instead of opening a new one. Maps to `...groupingConfiguration.reopenClosedIncident`.

grouping_lookback.description: Only group alerts raised within this window. Maps to `...groupingConfiguration.lookbackDuration`.

matching.description: `AllEntities` groups when every entity matches; `AnyAlert` groups everything this rule raises; `Selected` uses the `group_by_*` lists.

group_by_entities.description: Entity types to group on when `matching` is `Selected`. Only entities this rule maps may be used.

group_by_alert_details.description: Alert details to group on when `matching` is `Selected`. Maps to `...groupingConfiguration.groupByAlertDetails`.

group_by_custom_details.description: Custom detail keys to group on when `matching` is `Selected`. Only keys declared in `alert.custom_details` may be used.

entities.description: Entity mappings: how query columns become the accounts, hosts and IPs Sentinel builds investigation graphs from. At most 10 mappings, each with at most 3 identifiers and at least one strong one. Maps to `entityMappings`.

mappings.description: Field mappings for the Account entity. Needs at least one strong identifier: Sid, Name, FullName, AadUserId, PUID, ObjectGuid.

column.description: Query result column holding the value. Must exist in the query output.

entities_columns.description: Query result columns holding a pre-built entities JSON array, as `_ASim`/`_Im` parsers emit. Preview API only (`sentinelEntitiesMappings[].columnName`); a rule carrying it deploys through `2025-10-01-preview`.

exclusions.description: Tuning exclusions appended to the deployed query in order, each with a reason.

reason.description: Why this exclusion exists. Required so tuning decisions stay auditable.

let.description: KQL `let` bindings emitted before the exclusion query and referenceable from it. Values are inserted verbatim.

query.description: KQL appended to the base query.

advanced.description: Escape hatch for unmodelled Sentinel API properties. Passed through verbatim and unvalidated; prefer a modelled field.

duration.description: A duration in either the shorthand engineers type (`5m`, `1h`, `14d`, `2d1h30m`) or the ISO 8601 form the API returns (`PT5M`, `PT1H`, `P14D`, `P2DT1H30M`). Shape only: bounds are stated per field and enforced by the deployer, not the pattern, so a value outside them is a plan error rather than an unreadable file.

$comment: Lessons from v0.1.0: duration patterns enumerated the 5m..14d bounds (a `P2DT1H30M` the API returns was unrepresentable), `FileHas` was a typo for `FileHash`, `severity` offered a `critical` Sentinel does not have, and `alertSeverityColumnName` / `alertTacticsColumnName` / `sentinelEntitiesMappings` were unmodelled. Techniques and sub-techniques are deliberately absent: `threat.attack[]` carries them and the deployer splits `T####.###` across the API's `techniques` and `subTechniques` lists. The rule id is derived by the deployer, so it is not carried either.
